ANSWERS ITS SECOND "NOT ESTABLISHED" CLAUSE, AND NOTHING ELSE. That clause asks "whether the right home is `sync` or a separate loop debt class". It is answered, and answered the hard way: the home is NOT the sync row, and putting it there is precisely what made the sentence false. Computed per target, "N node(s) here have never been exported" is a claim about ONE FILE phrased as a claim about the SEAT, and on a seat with six records it fired five times, every time untruthfully, while the record holding all 3662 live nodes stayed silent. `sync_debt::unexported_work` now answers it once for the seat.

⭐ SO THE FACT ASKED THE RIGHT QUESTION AND THE FIRST IMPLEMENTATION PICKED THE WRONG ANSWER. It flagged the choice as unsettled on 2026-08-16; the aid shipped on the sync row on 2026-08-23 without the question being taken up; the defect that produced followed on 2026-09-03. The open clause was load-bearing and was passed over.

🛑 ITS OTHER NOT-ESTABLISHED CLAUSE IS UNTOUCHED — whether a count comparison alone is sufficient, since equal counts with different ids still pass. That is as open as it was, and the seat-level form inherits it unchanged.
